Thanks — Laura from Redwood legal here. I reviewed ProspectCorp's redlines and noted a few items we should clarify before DocuSign execution:

1) Subprocessor objection mechanics: propose the following contract language: Redwood will notify Customer of new subprocessors at least 30 days prior to onboarding; Customer will have 14 days from notice to object on reasonable, documented security grounds. If parties cannot agree within the 14-day window, Redwood will provide commercially reasonable mitigation steps.

2) Key management: For CMK (customer-managed keys) we need to confirm whether ProspectCorp requires HSM-backed keys via a cloud KMS or expects an on-prem split-key model. For cloud KMS we support AWS KMS and GCP KMS integrations; HSMs require architecture review and a Private deployment.

3) Data transfers / SCCs: Redwood will incorporate the EU SCCs as an annex. We will not adopt BCRs at this time. If you require additional data localization commitments, please specify the scope and affected data types.

I attached a DPA redline that accepts the majority of your edits and marks the CMK options as a required addendum. Please review and advise if the proposed subprocessor objection clause works.
